purpose: complete-package cross-check of the production thermal model (CalculiX on the explicit package mesh) against MOOSE on the identical problem, plus MOOSE on a uniformly refined copy for the discretization change

filemesh_formats..msh: Gmsh ASCII (GmshIO; versions >= 2.0, 2.2 used here; 3-D physical groups -> subdomains, lower-dimensional elements -> sidesets, then deleted)

moose.objects: AnisoHeatConduction, AnisoHeatConductionMaterial (diagonal k_ortho), BodyForce, ConvectiveHeatFluxBC, NodalValueSampler

cores.note: CalculiX assembles on 8 threads but its default SPOOLES factorization runs on one ('Using 1 cpu for spooles'), and its Newton loop factors twice for this linear problem

timing_method: wall clock of the solver process; 3 timed repeats after one untimed warm-up on the production mesh (median and range), one run on the refined copy; shared host, so load averages are recorded

mesh.label: graded h_xy = 1.1 mm grid, every in-plane interval split in 2

energy.note: the deck prints node coordinates to 1e-6 mm, so the power deposited on the solved mesh differs from the ledger total by +1.45e-08 (relative); both codes solve the deck

mesh.construction: every production hex split 2x2x2 at its edge midpoints (strictly nested; blocks, sources and films inherited)

discretization_change.what: MOOSE on the production mesh minus MOOSE on its uniform 2x2x2 refinement (identical problem); the production CalculiX solve equals the former

refinement_ladder.note: observed order and extrapolation from three strictly nested uniform refinements of the production mesh (h, h/2, h/3), identical problem

refinement_split.what: MOOSE on anisotropic refinements of the production mesh (nx, ny, nz children per hex), identical problem; changes are refined minus production mesh

inplane_ladder.what: in-plane refinement only (every in-plane interval of the production mesh split in n = 1, 2, 3, 4; through-thickness unchanged), identical problem; extrapolation from the finest three levels (generalized Richardson)

Z1.mesh: 144512 hex / 153873 nodes (graded h_xy = 1.1 mm grid, every in-plane interval split in 2)
Z1.cores: 8 CalculiX threads (SPOOLES factorization single-threaded); 8 MOOSE MPI ranks

Z3.mesh: 126536 hex / 135731 nodes (graded h_xy = 1.1 mm grid, every in-plane interval split in 2)
Z3.cores: 8 CalculiX threads (SPOOLES factorization single-threaded); 8 MOOSE MPI ranks

streamwise_film_within_column_sink_sprea.what: solve_thermal assigns each top face the coolant temperature after the heat of every face before it in an argsort on centroid x; faces sharing one x (one streamwise column) therefore get different sink temperatures, spread over the column's share of the coolant rise, although a 1-D coolant model gives them one
streamwise_film_within_column_sink_sprea.status: observation only; not part of the verification problem (uniform film)

z2_bga_temperature_region.what: temperature_regions('Z2')['bga'] selects by element-centroid z (production _layer_elems), so inside the PCB opening it also takes the converter elements that share the BGA's z range; the region feeds the ledger's BGA temperature, used only by the BGA-fed terms (the Z2BF control on this geometry)
z2_bga_temperature_region.status: observation only; Z1 and Z3 stacks do not overlap in z (unaffected)

caveats: The verification problem replaces the production streamwise top film (sink warming along the flow, 1-D coolant balance) by a uniform film at the inlet temperature with the same h; the streamwise coolant model itself is not cross-checked. It enters the deck through the same per-face *FILM lines verified here.

On the identical mesh both codes use trilinear hexahedra with exact quadrature on axis-aligned bricks, so their discrete systems coincide: that comparison verifies the deck (materials, anisotropy, sources, films, units) and the CalculiX solve, not the discretization. The refined MOOSE meshes measure the discretization error.
Both codes use the production homogenized material cards; the homogenizations are checked separately (unit-cell and RVE references), not here.
CalculiX prints nodal temperatures to 7 significant digits (1e-4 K above 100 C, 1e-5 K below), which bounds the measurable identical-mesh agreement.
The deck prints node coordinates to 1e-6 mm and conductivities to 6 significant digits; both codes solve the deck as printed (input audit).

Runtimes are wall clock on a shared 96-core host (load average 60-80) with 8 cores per solver; CalculiX's default SPOOLES factorization is single-threaded and its Newton loop factors twice for this linear problem.

Extrapolated mesh-converged values come from nested refinements with observed orders below 2 (the change is in-plane and sits in the converter stack and everything below it); they are estimates, not bounds.
